newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 7.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch- May 7.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** The Indian government is considering ways to reduce a growing "oil pool" deficit stemming from subsidised domestic prices, junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said on Tuesday.
"The ways and means of meeting the oil pool deficit is under the active consideration of the government," Balu told the lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha.

The oil pool account has fallen into deficit because the cost of subsidies keeping down the domestic prices of some petroleum products has not been fully offset by payments into the account from levies on non-subsidised petroleum products.

** Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, who also holds the petroleum portfolio, is expected to approve a draft cabinet note on oil price hike by the end of the week, the Financial Express newspaper reports.
The paper says a cabinet note, attempting a roughly 15 percent increase in the price of petroleum products, is being drafted to enable the government to announce a hike by the end of the month.

** Century Textiles & Industries Ltd, the flagship of the B.K. Birla group, shocked analysts by posting a 99 percent fall in 1996/97 (April-March) net profits to 26.7 million rupees from 1.95 billion last year.
The company blamed adverse market conditions in cement and paper and teething troubles at its Bagasse-based plant among the major factors for the steep fall in net profit.
The issue of one bonus equity share for every one share held by investors failed to lift the market gloom over the firm's poor results.
Shares of Century Textiles crashed nearly 13 percent from the day's high of 2,600 to 2,259.0 at the Bombay exchange, but ended 142 rupees, or six percent down over Monday's close.
** Indian Rayon & Industries Ltd, part of the Aditya Birla group said it would offer investors one bonus equity share for every two shares held.
The decision to issue bonus equity shares was taken at a board meeting. Indian Rayon shares lost 2.4 percent, to close at 393.0 rupees on Tuesday.
STOCKS TO WATCH:
Scooter giant, Bajaj Auto's net profit in 1996/97 (April-March) will be between 4.25-4.30 billion rupees according to company sources, the Financial Express newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The company posted a profit after tax of 4.18 billion rupees in 1995/96. Turnover was projected at 34.0 billion rupees, up 16 percent from 29.32 billion rupees in 1995/96.
The company's board is scheduled to meet on May 14 to settle the 1996/97 financial results and decide the dividend.
Bajaj Auto shares ended 22.25 rupees up at 880.0 at the Bombay exchange on Tuesday.
** Maharashtra Scooters is due to hold a board meeting later on Wednesday to finalise a bonus share issue and results for the year ending March 31, 1997.
Shares of Maharashtra Scooters closed 9.25 rupees lower at 239.75 rupees on Tuesday.
MARKETS:

** Indian shares ended broadly up in a choppy trading session on Tuesday, with action focussed only on select stocks amid continued worries about a possible increase in prices of petroleum products, dealers said.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index .BSESN gained 24.71 points, or 0.66 percent at 3,781.49.
** The 50-stock National exchange index .NSEI rose 2.90 points to 1,048.40.
-- Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
